maps.description:
After the Allies' breakthrough at El Alamein in October 1942 the New Zealand Division helped pursue retreating German-Italian forces along the Libyan coast.

On 23 January 1943 the New Zealanders were the first Commonwealth troops to enter the city of Tripoli. As soon as engineers and naval forces cleared the devastated port, men from the division helped unload supply ships carrying food and equipment needed for the 8th Army’s advance.

maps.description: 330-PSA-113-60-4:   Safety in North Africa.  En route to Brussels, Belgium, these refugees from the Republic of Congo found safety and comfort at Wheelus Air Force Base, Tripoli, Libya, after a flight from Brazzaville in a U.S. Air Force C-118 aircraft.  The plane was one of two MATS aircraft which moved a total of 175 refugees through Wheelus on July 13, 1960.  A Wheelus helicopter airlifted to the Congo helped in the evacuation. maps.title: 330-PSA-113-60-3 (20710528179).jpg
maps.author: National Museum of the U.S. Navy
maps.description: 330-PSA-113-60-3:   Refugees Land at Wheelus.  First step for these refugees from the strife-torn Congo to Wheelus Air Base, Tripoli, Libya.  They landed at 3 a.m. on July 13, 1960. By a U.S. Air Force C-124 of the 63d Troop Carrier Wing.  Carrying 89 persons, the big Globemaster ws one of two MATS planes making evacuation flights through Wheelus to the European continent.   The refugees were given medical attention, and briefed before taking off on the last leg of the mercy flight.   Shown here are some of the first to disembark from the C-124, which continued to Paris, France.   (8/25/2015).
